video_title: NBA on NBC Crew On Knicks’ Championship, Fatherhood & Their Sons’ Basketball Journeys

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' championship run and team belief
quotes.excerpt: Once that belief happened, I thought they would sacrifice for each other.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: At the beginning of the season, there was a lot of hype behind it. And then we got on and it was like, okay, we're not sure. There's a situation where Jalen Brunson was like, gave us the soundbite of, I'm not sure what I'm doing, to what it became. What are your thoughts about it real quick? It turned from, I'm not sure, to they can pull this off.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: That belief. Once that belief happened, I thought they would sacrifice for each other. But I'm more happy for the city to be honest with you. Because I actually played here and knowing what these fans went through, the fan base, how passionate they are, they're the most passionate fans in the world. So to see them celebrate a championship they haven't gotten since 73, I'm so happy for them.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' perfect storm playoff run
quotes.excerpt: It was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time.
quotes.quote: It was a perfect storm. They were down 2-1. People were looking at Jalen Brunson crazy. People were talking about benching Mikal Bridges. Why did we give up all these first-round picks for Mikal Bridges? And then they smacked them and tied it up in 2-2, and then they went on to win that series. It was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time. Obviously, you have the closer, the Derek Jeter, and Jalen Brunson and all that, but it was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time. And then obviously, Jalen Brunson reinventing himself as being a point center. He took less for them to win more, which was the chip. A perfect storm for the New York Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on the challenges of parenting a young basketball player
quotes.excerpt: I don't want to always tell him to do things because I want him to find that love.
quotes.quote: Being my son comes with a lot. Everywhere we go, people are doing this, or people are, you know, and I was one of those players that I loved doing all the boring things. I loved just being in the gym by myself, 100 left, 100 right, dribbling, whatever, shooting a thousand times. Those things are boring. In today's age, with so many gadgets and lights, kids don't like to do the boring things. So I say that because my son has all the talent. He was so much better than I was at 13, because I wasn't the athlete that he has. But it's the little things that will make the big things happen. I watch your kids' journeys and live through you to see, because I talk to Jamal a lot, how can I get him to go down to work on his own, to do push-ups, to do pull-ups? I don't want to always tell him to do things because I want him to find that love on his own.
